timing.both_saved_timing_notes: uart_roundtrip includes UART transfer, ARM control and FPGA work; excludes host RGB packing/reference/display. It is not PL latency or video FPS.
timing.current_client_interval: software/uart_image_client.py:191 through :217: after request packing/CRC, before first serial write; through complete response reception, protocol and response CRC validation. Excludes RGB packing, request-body CRC, NumPy reference, array conversion, saving and display.
timing.sample_design: 2 distinct fixed inputs x 5 modes per version; one timing sample for each input/mode pair; descriptive only

wire_time_model.interpretation: 8N1 line times are a lower-bound model excluding computation, USB/OS latency, gaps and protocol processing. The nominal model omits the old divisor rounding of +0.0064 percent. Agreement with observed timing identifies the main transfer bottleneck but does not isolate causal contributions of every firmware/host change.

limitations: This is a joint UART transport configuration and firmware-version comparison, not an isolated single-factor baud experiment and not a PL acceleration measurement.

The baseline main.c recovered from tmp/dma_poison_offline_20261031_084427_c9855a6c/main.before.c exactly matches the old manifest and is archived with matching start.S/link.ld in firmware/baselines/uart_115200. New sources are archived in the original 2M build/source_snapshot. Both archived source sets were rebuilt offline and produced byte-identical original ELF files. This establishes binary reproduction; historical host/loader source versions are still not embedded in each run result.

Verified source differences include explicit UART initialization/divisor selection and DMA reset-failure poison/cleanup guards. The original firmware already had DMA address readback checks. The entire timing difference must not be assigned exclusively to baud rate.

Both result.json files carry the same timing_note but no ELF, bit or host-source hashes. Run-to-build attribution uses the build directory, adjacent preflight/load logs, and the documented recovery chain; it is not an embedded per-run cryptographic binding.
New initial load.log records PL and PS initialization then an ELF-path failure; finish_download_20261101.log records the subsequent firmware-only download/start. The initial failure is preserved.
Same target device, PL 50 MHz and UART reference 100 MHz are verified configuration evidence. No independent per-run clock-register measurements or unique physical-board serial numbers are present.
The two samples per mode are two different fixed fixture images, not repeated randomized timing trials; no confidence interval or statistical significance is claimed.
NPZ files contain actual/expected/difference only. Input equality is independently verified using the per-run inputs/frameN.npy and .rgb files and the common 32-bit fixture source.
Resource counts are one routed implementation reused in both runs, not two separate synthesis/implementation measurements and not a resource reduction.
Offline audit only. No serial/JTAG/camera/GUI operation was performed and no original run report was modified.

The new offline rebuilds were not redeployed and are not new hardware measurements. Historic build-script source is not required to recover the tested ELF now that both archived source sets reproduce each original ELF byte for byte; host/loader experiment-environment differences remain outside that binary proof.
